posting.title: Head of Category – Grocery & FMCG
must_have: 8-12 years in category management, buying or merchandising in grocery, FMCG, quick-commerce or e-commerce
Has owned a category P&L of meaningful size with strong margin, pricing and inventory math
Experience negotiating with national FMCG brands and distributors
Hands-on with data: SQL or strong analyst partnership, dashboards, pricing benchmarks
Has built and led a team of 10+
Has worked closely with product/engineering on internal tools
Thrives in speed; Bengaluru-based or willing to relocate
nice_to_have: Experience launching a new city or region
company_language: work hand in hand with product and supply chain
the tools that run the category
joint business plans with top FMCG brands
red_flags: Scope is very broad for one role: assortment, pricing, promotions, supplier terms, inventory, team leadership and internal tooling across three cities
No salary or compensation information in the posting
"Thrives in speed" and "fastest grocery delivery" are vague and unquantified
Data requirement is ambiguous: "SQL or strong analyst partnership" does not say whether hands-on coding is expected

matches.requirement: 8-12 years in category management, buying or merchandising in grocery, FMCG, quick-commerce or e-commerce
matches.suggestion: Lead with the Ninjacart FMCG and Grocery directorship and the earlier category management roles (Ninjacart Chennai, Fashinza). Together they add up to roughly 7+ years in category management, and 10+ years overall. Use the posting's wording: 'category management in grocery and FMCG'.

matches.requirement: Has owned a category P&L of meaningful size with strong margin, pricing and inventory math
matches.evidence: Managed P&L for key categories contributing 60% of revenue, driving 5x growth in daily volumes within 100 days.
matches.suggestion: Pair this with the Ninjacart Director bullet on 'pricing strategies, inventory optimization, P&L management'. Add absolute figures (revenue size, margin %) where you can, as the résumé has none for Ninjacart. The Unacademy '$5M with an EBITDA of 20%' line shows margin discipline.

matches.requirement: Experience negotiating with national FMCG brands and distributors
matches.evidence: Business Side: End-to-end category management, product selection, market intelligence, pricing strategies, inventory optimization, P&L management, vendor negotiations, and retail strategy implementation.
matches.suggestion: 'Vendor negotiations' and 'Cultivated strong relationships with key brands and sellers' are generic. Name the national brands or distributors you dealt with, and mention any joint business plans or trade terms you secured. Don't claim JBPs unless you did them.

matches.requirement: Hands-on with data: SQL or strong analyst partnership, dashboards, pricing benchmarks
matches.evidence: Led P&L optimization and market intelligence for 30+ cities, conducting daily price benchmarking across 75+ SKUs.
matches.suggestion: Say 'daily competitive benchmarking' to match Zepto's wording. Also cite SQL, Tableau and Amplitude from the Technical Skills section, and the Accenture engineering background.

matches.requirement: Has built and led a team of 10+
matches.evidence: Led cross-functional teams of over 250 members across layers.
matches.suggestion: Make clear how many were direct reports versus indirect, and which team was in which role (e.g. category/buying team at Ninjacart). The 250 figure is cross-functional and could look inflated without that breakdown.

matches.requirement: Has worked closely with product/engineering on internal tools
matches.evidence: Product Side: Worked closely with the tech and engineering teams and product managed the entire development and deployment of the seller and buyer facing applications.
matches.suggestion: Say 'product managed seller and buyer apps with engineering' and note whether any were internal category or pricing tools. Zepto's 'tools that run the category' means internal tooling, so clarify if your apps fit that.

matches.requirement: Thrives in speed; Bengaluru-based or willing to relocate
matches.suggestion: You are Bengaluru-based. Back up 'thrives in speed' with '5x growth in daily volumes within 100 days' and 'Drove online revenue market share from 8% to a commanding 55% in just 18 months'.
No quick-commerce or dark-store experience appears. Don't claim it. Mention adjacent experience in fast-moving perishable and grocery supply at Ninjacart, with daily pricing and inventory decisions.

matches.requirement: Experience launching a new city or region
matches.evidence: Led P&L optimization and market intelligence for 30+ cities, conducting daily price benchmarking across 75+ SKUs.
matches.suggestion: This shows multi-city operations but not a launch. If you opened or scaled any city at Ninjacart, state it explicitly. Otherwise describe it as multi-city scaling, not launching.
Mention your CEG, Anna University B.E. in Computer Science and your three years as a Software Engineer at Accenture. This is a clear plus for working with product and engineering.

changes.what: Set headline to 'Head of Category, Grocery & FMCG'
changes.why: Matches the target role title instead of the current title.

changes.what: Replaced the Job Objective and Profile Summary with a 3-line posting-specific summary
changes.why: Removes generic wording ('results-driven') and leads with category P&L, benchmarking and product/engineering proof.

changes.what: Added a 'relevant' block mapping proof to the posting's P&L, pricing/data, product-engineering and brand/team requirements
changes.why: Recruiters see the must-have evidence at the top. Quick-commerce, dark-store and new-city launch are left out because the résumé has no evidence for them.

changes.what: Split the Ninjacart Director's two compressed bullets into five
changes.why: The original listed category management, pricing, inventory, P&L and vendor negotiation in one line. Unpacking them makes each posting keyword visible, with no new facts added.

changes.what: Split the Ninjacart (Chennai) bullets into three
changes.why: Separates the 60%-of-revenue P&L, the 30+ city market intelligence and the 75+ SKU daily price benchmarking, which map directly to the posting.

changes.what: Moved the 30% YoY revenue growth, 20% EBITDA and positive cash flow line from the Profile Summary into the Unacademy bullets
changes.why: It is proof of P&L discipline; it was buried in the summary.

changes.what: Reordered Unacademy bullets to lead with the portfolio and margin, market share and ROI, then assortments and engineering collaboration; merged the CLM and funnel bullets
changes.why: Puts P&L, assortment and product-collaboration evidence ahead of marketing-funnel detail.

changes.what: Cut the 'client feedback loop' bullet from Unacademy and Fashinza
changes.why: It is generic and duplicated across both roles; it doesn't answer any must-have.

changes.what: Cut the Unacademy bullet on top, mid and bottom-funnel content strategies as a separate item
changes.why: Performance-marketing detail is not what the posting asks for; the substance is kept in the merged CLM bullet.

changes.what: Trimmed skills to those relevant to the posting and dropped most soft skills and Microsoft Office
changes.why: Keeps SQL, Tableau, Amplitude, Google Analytics, category and P&L skills prominent.

changes.what: Kept all four ventures but shortened the wording, putting the revenue-generating ones (Valarlife, Fraternitee) first
changes.why: Shows commercial ownership; the failed or blocked ventures are kept short.
Relevant to a South-region role covering Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad.

changes.what: Removed personal-detail and generic language lines such as the 'Led cross-functional teams of over 250' claim from the summary block, and placed it in the relevant section instead
changes.why: Team size is a must-have, so it is stated where it is easy to find. It is not attributed to a specific role because the original didn't tie it to one.

rewrite.referral_note: Hi, I'm applying for the Head of Category – Grocery & FMCG role at Zepto in Bengaluru. I currently head the FMCG and Grocery vertical at Ninjacart. Earlier I ran P&L for categories contributing 60% of revenue and benchmarked prices daily across 75+ SKUs in 30+ cities. I'm also a Computer Science engineer who product-managed our buyer and seller apps. Could you refer me or point me to the hiring manager?
rewrite.fit_line: Strong on category P&L, daily price benchmarking, SQL/analytics, engineering background and a Bengaluru base; the gaps are quick-commerce or dark-store experience, launching a new city, and explicit evidence of negotiating with national FMCG brands, and your internal-tools experience is seller/buyer apps. Apply, but expect questions on those.

problems.claim: Category and P&L leader with 10 years across category management, growth and engineering
problems.reason: The original shows 10 years total, but only about 3 years (Sep'14 to Aug'17) were in engineering. The phrasing implies 10 years of engineering experience.

problems.claim: Brands and teams: vendor negotiations and key brand and seller relationships at Ninjacart
problems.reason: The original lists 'Cultivated strong relationships with key brands and sellers' in the general Profile Summary without tying it to Ninjacart. Attributing it to Ninjacart is an unsupported employer attribution.
